item.title: Wife of top Burnham adviser backs Sally Rooney after books withdrawn over Palestine Action support
item.description:
Wife of top Burnham adviser backs Sally Rooney after books withdrawn over Palestine Action support

Submitted by Imran Mulla on Fri, 10/16/2026 - 14:44
Sarah Helm, a prominent author and journalist, is the wife of the British prime minister's national security adviser, Jonathan Powell
Sarah Helm is a former foreign correspondent for The Independent and has been a longtime critic of the Israeli government's policies towards Palestinians (Screengrab/X)
Off

Sarah Helm, a prominent author and the wife of UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's national security adviser, has posted on X in support of Sally Rooney, whose books are being withdrawn from the UK market over her support of Palestine Action.

Helm is the wife of Jonathan Powell, who served as former prime minister Keir Starmer's adviser on national security, foreign policy and intelligence - and remained in the role when Burnham become prime minister.

Responding to the journalist Adam Boulton, who on Sky News on Thursday criticised Rooney and accused her of taking a "very strong pro-Palestine, and, I have to say, anti-Israel and anti-Jewish stance", Helm posted: "God help us authors who support Palestine and Palestine Action.  Sounds like Adam would have all our books swept off the shelves in a jiffy."

Powell, who was formerly a senior official under Tony Blair's premiership, reportedly opposed Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband's decision to sanction Israeli settlements last month.

His wife Helm is a former foreign correspondent for The Independent newspaper and has been a longtime critic of the Israeli government's policies towards Palestinians. 

Helm is the author of the 2025 book Gaza: The Long Road to Destruction, 1870-2024, a history of Gaza which includes interviews with survivors of the 1948 Nakba. 

She has also previously written for Middle East Eye.

Pro-Israel groups call for police investigation

Helm is now facing calls for a police investigation by pro-Israel groups including the Campaign Against Antisemitism.

Keir Starmer's Labour government proscribed Palestine Action in July 2025, meaning that expressing support for or membership of the direct action group - which aimed to cause property damage to companies manufacturing weapons that would be sold to Israel - is a criminal offence that could lead to a prison sentence of up to 14 years.

The ban has been widely denounced as draconian by human rights organisations.

Thousands of people have been arrested since it came into effect for holding placards expressing support for the group.

Earlier this week it emerged that bestselling author Sally Rooney is being forced to withdraw her books from sale in the UK because she said after Palestine Action was banned that she would use proceeds from her book sales to support it.

The novelist said on Wednesday: "I wrote an opinion piece expressing my intention to go on supporting Palestine Action, which is not a proscribed or otherwise prohibited group here in the Republic of Ireland.

"As a result, the fulfilment of contracts to publish my work in the UK could now constitute a serious criminal offence."

Rooney cancelled a trip to England last September to collect a literary award over the fear of being arrested.

Sally Rooney's books to be withdrawn from sale in UK over Palestine Action support
Read More »

The case is due to be heard at the Supreme Court later this year.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said last month that Andy Burnham's government is “looking at” whether the ban on Palestine Action was politically sensible, arguing that the government had not intended for mass arrests to take place by implementing the proscription.

He argued: "I don’t think anyone’s intent was to have those people criminalised, but obviously the Supreme Court has got to look at this issue, and obviously it’s something we keep looking at as government."

Kerry Moscogiuri, the chief executive of Amnesty International UK, told The Guardian: "Whatever one’s views on Palestine Action, we should all be concerned when laws intended to combat terrorism end up silencing artistic freedom and the ability to engage in peaceful political dissent.

"Writers should not find their books disappearing from shelves because of their political beliefs.

"Nor should people have to choose between expressing their conscience and pursuing their livelihoods."

item.title: Palestinians wounded, US journalist hospitalised after coordinated attack by masked Israeli setters
item.description:
Palestinians wounded, US journalist hospitalised after coordinated attack by masked Israeli setters

Submitted by MEE staff on Fri, 10/16/2026 - 14:29
Washington Post journalist Heidi Levine said she was kicked to the ground and beaten 'probably 50 times' by settlers clad in black
Heidi Levine, a photojournalist with the Washington Post, speaks to journalists at the hospital after sustaining multiple injuries during an attack by Israeli militant settlers on Palestinians harvesting olives, in Ramallah in the Israeli-occupied West Bank (Reuters)
Off

Palestinians attempting to gather their olive harvests and an American photojournalist have been wounded in an attack by a masked mob of Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.

Witnesses reported that some 80 settlers, masked and clad in black, descended on the village of Abu Falah in northeast Ramallah, slinging rocks at Palestinian families picking olives and setting the groves alight.

Video footage circulated online showed Washington Post journalist Heidi Levine being knocked to the ground and repeatedly beaten by settlers with sticks. 

The reporter was hospitalised after the incident, along with another Palestinian, medics said.

Speaking from her hospital bed with a bandaged hand and her voice shaking, Levine told reporters: "I was attacked, pushed to the ground. Luckily I had my flak jacket and helmet, otherwise I probably wouldn't even be here, because they just kept kicking me and kicking me, probably fifty times.

"After like 10 minutes they tried to get me stand up and then they pushed me down again and continued to kick me. I was trying to hold on to my cameras and my pouch...they eventually broke everything off of me," she said.

Israeli guards ‘crushed’ Palestinian prisoner’s testicle with rubber bullet
Read More »

In a statement, Post executive editor Matt Murray called for a “thorough investigation” into the attack, emphasising that Levine was “wearing visible markings clearly identifying her as a journalist”.

Isreali journalist and activist Andrey Khrzhanovskiy, who filmed the assault, told the Post that Israeli soldiers arrived shortly before the attack, firing tear gas at Palestinians and doing “absolutely nothing about the settlers”.

Oren Ziv, an Israeli journalist who also witnessed the attack, said one Palestinian was wounded by gunfire, while Reuters reported that at least one of the settlers carried a firearm.

Jasper Nathaniel, another American journalist who was at the scene, reported "machine gunfire" with at "least one Palestinian shot".

"If she didn’t have a helmet - and if she was Palestinian - she could be dead," Nathaniel said in a post on X.

Wafa news agency reported that Israeli settlers assaulted a 70-year-old Palestinian man and smashed several Palestinian-owned vehicles during an attack on olive pickers near the town of Birzeit, north of Ramallah.

Local sources said the elderly man was left with fractures and other injuries following the assault.

item.title: Hamas accuses Mladenov of siding with Israel over Gaza goods dispute
item.description:
Hamas accuses Mladenov of siding with Israel over Gaza goods dispute

Hamas has rejected accusations from Board of Peace Director-General Nickolay Mladenov over halted commercial deliveries to Gaza, saying he repeated Israel’s account.

In a statement on Friday, the group dismissed his accusation of “coercion,” calling his position “blatant bias and complicity with the occupation and its pretexts aimed at obstructing the entry of goods”.

Mladenov wrote on social media on Thursday that Israel’s Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT) had sent him a report blaming Hamas for the suspension.

COGAT operates under Israel’s defence ministry and oversees civilian affairs in the Palestinian territories.

item.title: Spanish-built combat vehicles for Latvia to carry Israeli turrets despite arms embargo
item.description:
Spanish-built combat vehicles for Latvia to carry Israeli turrets despite arms embargo

A Spanish arms company has begun delivering infantry fighting vehicles fitted with Israeli weapons systems to Latvia, despite the Spanish government declaring an arms embargo on Israel last year, Israeli business daily Globes reported on Thursday.

According to the report, Latvia ordered 84 of the vehicles last year from General Dynamics European Land Systems-Santa Barbara Sistemas (GDELS-SBS), which is headquartered in Madrid, in a deal worth around €800m ($929m), with all the vehicles due to be delivered by 2029.

The infantry fighting vehicles, called Mednieks, are equipped with unmanned turret systems, called UT30 MK2, which are produced by the Israeli arms company Elbit Systems.

“The delivery of infantry fighting vehicles is a significant step toward strengthening Latvia’s defence capabilities,” Latvia’s Defence Minister Raivis Melnis said last week, adding that the Mednieks would reinforce his country’s armed forces “as well as promote cooperation between the National Armed Forces and Nato allies”.

item.title: Human Rights Watch warns 50 detainees face imminent execution in eastern Libya
item.description: Human Rights Watch (HRW) has warned that at least 50 detainees face imminent execution at Gernada military prison in eastern Libya, after forces led by Khalifa Haftar reportedly executed at least 31 people following military trials that the organisation described as seriously unfair. In a statement dated 14th October, the rights organization said the Libyan Arab Armed Forces had carried out the executions since late August 2026, raising concerns about further death sentences being implemented. According to HRW, the executions were the first known instances of capital punishment in Libya since 2010, ending a de facto moratorium on executions that had lasted approximately 15 years.
